summary: The registered analysis estimates the whole-hypothalamus HFD-versus-chow effect in 15 wild-type males. Garrett et al.’s Supplementary Table S6 estimates the diet effect across those mice and 17 Gpr101 knockout males. The other gene lists, labelled figure panels and public deposits yielded no author-reported WT-specific diet effect.

manualReview.summary: GEO confirms the wild-type libraries. Supplementary Table S6 combines wild-type and knockout mice.
manualReview.note: GSE220533 contains one bulk hypothalamus library per male mouse, collected at 21 weeks. The registered sample sheet selects all 7 WT chow and 8 WT HFD libraries, and limma estimates the HFD-minus-chow difference in mean deposited log2-normalized expression. Garrett et al. used DESeq2 after low-expression filtering. Their Table S6 reports 327 signed linear HFD-versus-chow fold changes selected at adjusted P < 0.1 across both genotypes, including 8 KO chow and 9 KO HFD mice. Tables S2–S5 report genotype effects and a genotype-by-diet interaction. Fig. 1A reports a genotype test for Gpr101, and Fig. S3 shows sample-level expression. The series CSV and individual GSM files contain normalized expression. The separate GEO series matrix has zero feature rows. The independently retrieved GEO matrix and registered DE table each match the SHA-256 recorded for them in the run provenance. The local raw-input path was absent. See data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE220533/codex-2026-11-24/SEARCH_LOG.md and data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE220533/codex-2026-11-24/SOURCES.tsv.
reviewFlags: No WT-specific diet coefficient was located in the reviewed author sources. Tables S2 through S6 give selection cutoffs and fold changes for other contrasts. They omit individual raw and adjusted P values.
The legacy analysis has no committed source-file checksum manifest. The GEO download matches the input checksum in the fit provenance.

verificationReview.reason: Supplementary Table S6 reports HFD relative to chow across WT and Gpr101 knockout males. The registered limma coefficient estimates that diet difference within the 15 WT males. Tables S2 through S4 compare genotypes, S5 gives the genotype-by-diet interaction, and the enrichment workbook reports term-level statistics. The expression figures and GEO deposits supply no author-reported coefficient for the WT diet contrast.
verificationReview.nextStep: Reopen when an author-produced WT HFD-versus-chow gene result identifies the included libraries, direction and effect scale, or the authors release their fitted model with sufficient coding to extract that simple effect. Record any model-derived extraction separately. A selected result covers only its reported genes.
